Achillea (Yarrow): Mildly toxic - leaves, stems, and flowers/all above-ground parts are toxic; treat the whole plant as unsafe for dogs
Actaea (Baneberry): Highly toxic - all parts are toxic, especially the berries and roots
Allium (Onion family): Highly toxic - all parts and all forms are toxic (bulbs, leaves/greens, raw, cooked, dried, or powdered)
Aquilegia: Mildly toxic - seeds and roots are the most toxic; rest of plant may also cause GI upset
Baptisia: Mildly toxic - all parts contain toxic alkaloids, with roots, seeds, and seed pods the main concern
Bigleaf Hydrangea: Mildly toxic - all parts are toxic, especially leaves, buds, and flowers
Hydrangea: Mildly toxic - all parts, especially flower buds and young leaves
Helleborus: Mildly toxic - all parts, especially the roots
Ilex (Holly): Mildly toxic - berries and leaves are the main toxic parts
Japanese Anemone: Mildly toxic - all fresh sap-containing parts (leaves, stems, flowers, roots)
Mountain Laurel: Highly toxic - all parts, including leaves, stems, flowers, nectar and pollen
Pieris: Highly toxic - all parts, especially the leaves
Rhododendron: Highly toxic - all parts, including leaves, stems, flowers, pollen and nectar
Tomato: Mildly toxic - leaves, stems/vines, flowers, and unripe green fruit are toxic; ripe red fruit is safe
Solomon's Seal: Mildly toxic - all parts are considered toxic, especially berries and rhizomes
Parsley: Mildly toxic only in large amounts - seeds/oil have highest concern; small culinary amounts are low-risk
Yew: Highly toxic - needles/leaves, bark/wood, and seeds are toxic; only the red fleshy aril is non-toxic
Arborvitae: Mildly toxic - primarily foliage/scale leaves, twigs/bark, sap, and essential oil
Carnation: Mildly toxic - above-ground parts (flowers/petals, leaves, stems) cause mild GI upset
Egyptian Walking Onion: Highly toxic - all parts are toxic, including bulbs, bulbils, leaves, stems, and flowers
Single Mum: Mildly toxic - all parts are toxic, including flowers, leaves, stems, and roots
